articles.title: OPENAI TESTING NEW "AURORA" GPT-IMAGE MODEL ON ARENA
articles.summary: Three new model references briefly appeared in OpenAI's API and in blind arena tests this weekend. aurora-red-alpha, aurora-green-alpha, and aurora-blue-alpha appear to be image models and could possibly be GPT Image 3. In tests, red ran faster than green but was lower quality, while green was slower but looked better. Examples of images generated by the models are available in the article.

articles.title: SEARCH & FETCH
articles.summary: DeepSeek's Search and Fetch APIs give agents and RAG applications access to live web content. The Search API finds web pages for a query and returns structured results. The Fetch API retrieves a single web page and returns its content as Markdown. Both are raw JSON APIs. They use the same bearer authentication as the DeepSeek API.

articles.title: DEEPSEEK-V4.1-FLASH-1017 (HUGGING FACE REPO)
articles.summary: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 delivers substantial improvements across reasoning, coding, agentic tasks, and visual benchmarks. It also reduces task execution time and output length, advancing the performance-cost Pareto frontier across multiple agent harnesses. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash combines cross-layer KV cache reuse in Compressed Sparse Attention 2 with FP4 KV caching, reducing its global KV cache footprint to 890 bytes per token. Its persistent KV cache footprint is roughly 1/8 of that of DeepSeek-V4-Flash. The model delivers substantially better performance than the baseline despite its much smaller KV cache footprint.

articles.title: HOW THE CLAUDE CODE TEAM DOES CODE REVIEW
articles.summary: The Claude Code team has restructured its code review process to handle increased volume efficiently by automating most review stages. Key changes include continuous review, automated verifications, multi-layer checks before human intervention, and a tiered risk system for approvals.

articles.title: A BENCHMARK MAP OF THE US ECONOMY
articles.summary: The Benchmark Map is a project aimed at building a comprehensive, continuously updated resource for understanding AI capabilities across the economy. Initial findings suggest that 90% of American working hours are spent on tasks with little or no coverage from existing benchmarks. This makes it very hard to know how good AI models are at the work Americans actually do.
